items.title: Roger Kellaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: I was playing with Dick Wetmore, who is really an unknown to most people who taught me who Django Reinehardt was

ctx.x: So you went to the guidance counselor at Newton High School and she says, “What do you want to do?” At that point in your musical development did you have a specific idea of how you wanted to make your living in music?

No, I didn’t. But I did have a specific idea that it was going to be music. That happened when I was 12. I didn’t know exactly where it was going, yes I was daydreaming all the time waiting for the gigs on weekends, and by the time I was 16 I was then playing in Boston and playing Dixieland. I was meeting Ruby Braff, I was playing with Dick Wetmore, who is really an unknown to most people who taught me who Django Reinehardt was, he played cornet, violin and baritone horn and still does. Prodigy violinist…
Spike Jones. Spike Jones is a great thing to be influenced by. What did you like about Spike Jones?
